correctness.rationale: The two inequalities follow from the actual definition. Since every \(\Gamma\)-invariant probability is \(H\)-invariant, the first inequality is immediate. For the reverse bound, averaging any \(H\)-invariant measure over a full left-coset transversal gives a \(\Gamma\)-invariant measure even when \(H\) is not normal. Refining a cover jointly over the \(m\) coset translates and iterating Meyerovitch's pointwise cover-order Lemma 2.4 gives an \(H\)-cover whose integrated order is at most \(m\) times the corresponding \(\Gamma\)-order, hence \(\dim(X,T|_H)\le m\dim(X,T)\). The empty-measure case is simultaneous by the same coset averaging. The cyclic-layer sharpness example factors through the free finite quotient \(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z\), so Meyerovitch's finite-group formula gives \(d/m\), while the \(m\mathbb Z\)-restriction is trivial and has dimension \(d\). Boundary cases \(m=1\), infinite dimension, and empty invariant-measure simplices are correctly separated.
